headline: Maui Planning Commission Defers Mākena State Park SMA Permit

meeting.body: Maui Planning Commission Defers Mākena State Park SMA Permit
meeting.summary: The Maui Planning Commission adopted a written decision 5–2, denied a late petition to intervene, and deferred the Mākena State Park permit to July 14.
meeting.recap: The planning department reported it already approved a time extension, to April 30, 2027, for a bridge repair permit.[[0:04:29]] Restroom wastewater would be held in underground tanks and trucked away for treatment.[[1:02:39]] The state said the plan includes no fencing, reservation system or shuttle-only access.[[1:03:57]] One testifier supported permanent restrooms, saying people now leave toilet paper in the bushes.[[2:31:05]] A wildlife group leader said it is the most successful turtle nesting beach they monitor on Maui.[[3:18:33]] A former lifeguard lieutenant said the beach leads the state in spinal injuries.[[4:11:00]] With eight votes, the commission denied a late-filed petition to intervene (a request to join the case as a formal party).[[5:25:27]] The state said parking would grow from 238 to 276 spaces, about 13 percent.[[5:29:16]] The state apologized for installing two booths and three pay stations without SMA approval.[[5:45:54]] The commission voted six in favor to defer the permit to July 14 so the state can answer its questions.[[7:19:44]]
decided: A motion to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion) failed because no one seconded it.
The commission added lack of proper service and an unpaid filing fee as reasons to deny the petition to intervene.
The commission added as a reason that the petitioner told staff she wanted to withdraw and was not present.
SMA permit request by Bamboo Living on behalf of the Gay Family Trust: Item A3 was rescheduled to the August 11 meeting with no objection.
SMA permit request by G70 on behalf of Paradise Owner LLC for resort improvements: Item A2 was rescheduled to the August 25 meeting with no objection.
meeting.next: The state is to answer in writing on a bike path, resident parking, court status, sewer connection, a carrying capacity study, pervious paving, lighting and fire truck access. The July 14 agenda includes Mākena State Park, an appeal, a decision for a solar project, and an introduction to rewriting the zoning code.

moments.q: Staff says the petitioner wants to withdraw
"That was a misstep on our part though."
